description: The motor neurons of his six legs, pool by pool, and the knee sensors of each pair of legs, as the dataset names them. Facts only: which neurons, which leg, which side. What each muscle does to a leg, and how hard a moving knee drives its sensors, come from papers and from us, and live in the movement codec, not here. Front-leg groups gate the census because the ceremony's handling is done with the front legs.

evidence.claim: Bound by annotated type (SNpp39, SNpp41), class mechanosensory_proprioceptive, subclass chordotonal organ, entering by the front leg nerve ProLN: 8 SNpp39, 2 SNpp41. SNpp39: 2 of 39 neurons carry the dataset's synonym 'FeCO hook', all of them in the hind leg nerve, and none carries another organ's name; SNpp41: 3 of 22 neurons carry the dataset's synonym 'FeCO hook', all of them in the hind leg nerve, and none carries another organ's name. Members without the synonym, which is every front and middle-leg one, are taken to be the same kind because the dataset gives them the same type name.
evidence.source: MaleCNS v1.0 body annotations (columns type, class, entryNerve, synonyms, rootSide)

roles.explain: Sensory neurons of the front legs' femoral chordotonal organ, the stretch sensor of the knee, of the kind the dataset calls hook: they fire while the knee moves.
roles.caveat: The link from type to 'hook' or 'claw' is thin: a handful of labelled hind-leg neurons per type, for SNpp51 a single one. What hook and claw neurons respond to was measured in the front leg of female flies by calcium imaging (Mamiya, Gurung and Tuthill 2018), not in these cells. A neuron here has no cell body in the volume, so its side is the side its axon enters on.

roles.caveat: The link from type to 'hook' or 'claw' is thin: a handful of labelled hind-leg neurons per type, for SNpp51 a single one. notes.title: Named only in the front leg
notes.text: Tarsus levator and depressor and the tergopleural promotor carry a muscle name only in the front leg. In the middle and hind legs the corresponding neurons, if traced, are among the serially named ones.

notes.title: Their transmitter hardly matters here
notes.text: Fly motor neurons release glutamate at the muscle. Their transmitter label matters only for the few synapses they make inside the cord.

notes.title: The front leg's sensors are thin here
notes.text: The front leg nerve holds far fewer typed chordotonal neurons in this dataset than the middle and hind leg nerves. That is a fact about the reconstruction, not about the fly, and the page says so where it counts them.

notes.title: Not bound: club neurons and the unnamed types
notes.text: Club neurons (SNpp40, 47, 56, 57, 60) sense vibration, and a cartoon leg makes none. Chordotonal types with no synonym anywhere (SNpp42, 43, 44, 46, 48, 49, 58, 59) are left alone: a name is not a function.
